Is your green pipeline real?

Argus links JSM incidents to linked Bitbucket work, fires a synthetic canary to expose fake-green gates, and returns a re-verified repair patch. This command center runs the same twenty Elenchos rules as the Forge app, in your browser, on text you control.

Status: demo build. It evaluates the Bitbucket Pipelines YAML below directly in your browser. It does not connect to your Atlassian site and sends nothing anywhere.

Findings by Pipeline Stage & Control Domain

Normalized CI + SAST + Governance
Stage 1: Container & Runner Supply Chain (r01, r11, r14, r17, r20) 2/5 passing
Checks immutable image digests, Docker privilege, cache key pinning, pipe tags, and memory bounds.
Stage 2: Test & Exit-Code Integrity (r02, r03, r06, r12, r15) 1/5 passing
Catches masked exit codes (|| true, || exit 0), --passWithNoTests, set +e, and unbounded step timeouts.
Stage 3: Secrets, OIDC & Clone Hygiene (r04, r08, r13, r18, r19) 2/5 passing
Verifies OIDC role tokens, secret log masking, shallow git clone depth, artifact expiry, and branch checks.
Stage 4: Release & Security Gates (r05, r07, r09, r10, r16) 2/5 passing
Enforces production deployment locks, SAST/SCA gates, parallel step isolation, and PR branch triggers.

Execution Spine · JSM Incident DEMO-11

Deterministic Core
  1. 1. Bitbucket Pipeline #482 Ingested commit-9f2c41e

    Detected green deployment badge followed 7 minutes later by JSM P1 incident DEMO-11.

  2. 2. Elenchos 20-Rule Socratic Canary exit 1

    Exposed masked test failures (--passWithNoTests || true) and floating node:latest image.

  3. 3. SupportTrace 7-Source Evidence Seal 7/7 grounded

    Sealed provenance chain from DEMO-11 back to commit-9f2c41e with SHA-256 Merkle root.

  4. 4. PolicyShield Lachesis & Typed Change IR confirm

    Synthesized content-addressed repair patch and bound write approval to 64-char SHA-256 digest.

  5. 5. Standby On-Call Routing & Braille Receipt Merkle + Braille

    Enforced 900s SLA failover window and issued spoken + Grade-1 Braille audit receipt.

Exit 1 means at least one rule failed on these facts. Exit 0 means all
            twenty passed on the facts the extractor could see. One fact, required merge check
            enforcement (r13), lives in Bitbucket branch restrictions, not in this file, so here
            it stays flagged until the app reads it from the API. Each rule earned its id by
            separating a violating fixture (exit 1) from a clean one (exit 0) in the Socratic
            Kill-Test. A check that cannot separate the two is thrown out before a human sees it.
